methodology: Shear rheology experiments were conducted to investigate the rheological response of different series of poly(ethylene oxide) / silica (PEO/SiO2) nanocomposites with varying molecular weights and nanoparticle sizes, concentrations, and compositions.
research_objective: To understand the effect of nanoparticle size and concentration on the rheological properties of PEO/SiO2 nanocomposites and to investigate their potential for improving polymer properties.

key_findings.finding: A significant reduction of melt viscosity is observed due to a dilution of the entanglement network of polymer chains caused by the presence of nanoparticles.
The effect of nanoparticle size and concentration on rheological properties of PEO/SiO2 nanocomposites was investigated.
The state of dispersion of nanoparticles within the polymer matrix can affect the rheological and mechanical properties of nanocomposites.
Mechanical reinforcement in well-dispersed PEO/SiO2 hybrids is attributed to disentanglement of polymer chains rather than plasticization by nanoparticles.
Nanoparticle-polymer interactions result in reduced segmental mobility at low nanoparticle loadings.
At high nanoparticle loadings, a percolated network is formed leading to 'weak gel-like' behavior and increased activation energy.
The viscosity of polymer nanocomposites shows a non-Einstein-like decrease at higher nanoparticle concentrations, attributed to fluidification.
The incorporation of nanoparticles into polymer matrices can induce fluidification behavior, leading to a decrease in complex viscosity and polymer melt viscosity.

In this work, we investigate the rheological response of different series of poly(ethylene oxide) / silica, PEO/SiO2, nanocomposites by shear rheology. More specifically, spherical SiO2 nanoparticles of two different radii are dispersed in PEOs of different molecular weights covering the regime from unentangled to highly-entangled systems. Nanocomposites over a wide range of compositions were developed in order to investigate both the effect of the size and concentration of the nanoparticles and the effect of the molecular weight of the polymer matrix, on the rheological properties of the nanocomposite materials.
